- When sentiment is negative and historical prices are trending downward, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model overestimates short-term volatility when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — smooth 3-day moving average before forecasting.
- When sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
- Forecast horizon >15 days: model tends to overestimate upward bias — apply 3–5% downward adjustment if sentiment remains negative.
- If sentiment is negative and model forecast is >+5% above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overconfidence bias.
